agent_answer.notes: Only 9 of the 20 corpus papers report a hallucination / unsupported-statement / invented-fact rate; the other 11 papers do not measure hallucination. S007, S012 and S017 report their values in mixed units (fractions such as 0.399, counts per 1,000 such as 391, and percentages); values were normalized to percentages for comparison. S008 and S018 use condition codes: in S008 R is the retrieval-augmented generator and B the vanilla LLM; in S018 R is the retrieve-then-read model and B the vanilla LLM. No paper reports uncertainty estimates for these rates. Supporting claims: claim-000001 through claim-000027.

cells.conclusion: S001 (Legal Question Answering: A Controlled Comparison): chain-of-thought prompting has the lowest hallucination rate at 9.4% (vs. retrieval-augmented 17.8%, parametric-only 29.5%, fine-tuned 47.1%)
S006 (Hallucination Rate on PopCultureQA Across Model Designs): the fine-tuned model has the lowest hallucination rate at 9.8% (vs. RAG 18.3%, vanilla 21.5%)

S007 (Three Conditions on a Factual Question Benchmark): the generator adapted to the domain by further training has the lowest unsupported-statement rate at 18.2% (vs. no-document 39.1% and lookup 39.9%)

facts.s: S007 generator adapted to the domain by further training

cells.conclusion: S008 (Grounded Generation on Science Questions): R (retrieval-augmented generator) has the lowest hallucination rate at 6.3% (vs. B vanilla LLM 20.2%)
S010 (Passage Order in Trivia Answering): RAG without reranking has the lowest hallucination rate at 23.1% (vs. RAG with reranking 28.9%, retrieval-augmented 32.3%, vanilla 38.1%)
S012 (Two Conditions on a News Fact Benchmark): the model that answers from its own parameters has the lowest unsupported-statement rate at 19.3% (vs. retrieval-first 29.2%)

facts.s: S012 model that answers from its own parameters

cells.conclusion: S016 (Hallucination Frequency on HistoryQuest Under Alternative Lookup Designs): the retrieval-augmented generator has the lowest hallucination frequency at 5.1% (vs. no-retrieval 10.3%, query-rewriting 30.4%, RAG with random 41.2%)

S017 (Invented Facts Across Generator Conditions on Popular Culture Questions): the model that samples several answers and votes has the lowest invented-fact rate at 19.1% (vs. grounded-in-retrieved 31.4%, LM-alone 39.2%)

facts.s: S017 model that samples several answers and votes

cells.conclusion: S018 (Hallucination Rate in Two Answer Conditions): R (retrieve-then-read model) has the lowest hallucination rate at 16.3% (vs. B vanilla LLM 20.8%)

question: Which method achieves the lowest hallucination rate within each paper?
